pr_title: Fix Issue 620 - Incorrect IND(ADDR(LCL_VAR)) folding when types do not match
pr_body:
Fixes for morphing a GT_IND of a GT_ADDR of a GT_LCL_VAR
When the GT_IND size is a small type.
We can have a GT_IND as either a load or as a store,
it is a store when it is on the Left-Hand-Side of an assignment
Otherwise it is a load

The test case provide with this PR covers the various combinations that were incorrect.

issue_context.title: Incorrect IND(ADDR(LCL_VAR)) folding when types do not match
issue_context.body:
I was looking at reimplementing this kind of folding in `LocalAddressVisitor` and ran into this morph code:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f621f44cfad59eade2d263a19f39f38f7dc4a51b/src/coreclr/src/jit/morph.cpp#L12859-L12870

I don't think that "signed/unsigned differences won't matter":

```C#
static void Main() => Test(-1, 1);

[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
static unsafe void Test(short a, int b)
{
    short c = (short)(a * 2);
    int d = *((ushort*)&c) / b;
    Console.WriteLine(d);
}
```
generates
```asm
G_M41262_IG01:
       4883EC28             sub      rsp, 40
       448BC2               mov      r8d, edx
G_M41262_IG02:
       480FBFC1             movsx    rax, cx
       D1E0                 shl      eax, 1
       480FBFC0             movsx    rax, ax
       99                   cdq
       41F7F8               idiv     edx:eax, r8d
       8BC8                 mov      ecx, eax
       E8A4FCFFFF           call     System.Console:WriteLine(int)
       90                   nop
G_M41262_IG03:
       4883C428             add      rsp, 40
       C3                   ret
```
and prints [edit] -2. The result is obviously incorrect, `ushort / 1` can't ever be negative.

category:correctness
theme:morph
skill-level:intermediate
cost:medium
